result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers correctly blame proportional figures, give a tabular-nums fix you can paste, keep Gill Sans and say that tnum support depends on the font. B does better on alignment: it explains that place-value alignment also needs right alignment and consistent formatting, though its point about the comma is a bit muddled. A adds the useful lining-nums and unicode-range ideas, but it suggests other families as fallbacks and barely discusses alignment. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly blame proportional figures and give the same tabular-nums fix that can be pasted in. B is more honest about font support: it doesn't overclaim that Gill Sans MT has tnum and gives concrete fallbacks, including a digits-only font via unicode-range. A's point about commas is muddled: with right alignment, 240 and 119 still line up, so the comma doesn't break that. B suggests other families only as a fallback, but neither answer says much about alignment and digit counts.
